tools.name: jq
tools.$comment: jq fits the 'download our own copy' rubric (single ~2MB binary, no OS integration, slow release cadence). See plugins/bootstrap/skills/bootstrap/references/dependency-philosophy.md.

tools.name: claude
tools.$comment: Bootstrap drives marketplace and plugin lifecycle through the `claude` CLI, so the standalone CLI is a hard dependency -- not merely 'nice to have because the user is obviously running Claude'. The VS Code extension bundles a PRIVATE copy for its chat panel and deliberately does not put `claude` on PATH (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/vs-code), so an extension-only machine reaches this entry with no resolvable CLI and every marketplace/plugin step fails. Use the native installer rather than winget/brew: only native installs auto-update in the background (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup), so a package-manager copy would go stale forever and we would own that. The native installer lands the binary in ~/.local/bin, which installPath resolves directly -- that is also what lets the engine link the directory onto PATH after the install (see _link_tool_dir_to_path), instead of waiting for a PATH change to propagate into the already-running session.
